projectDetails.name: ZKsync
projectDetails.description: ZKsync is a zk-rollup ecosystem on Ethereum that uses zero-knowledge proofs to provide fast, cheap transactions with native EVM compatibility (on ZKsync Era).

topRisks.content: Lack of continuous on-chain monitoring lets abnormal fund flows go undetected, increasing the risk of delayed incident response.
Missing CCSS certification leaves crypto custody controls unvalidated, increasing the risk of undetected security gaps.

recentChanges.content: The new token audit, with all findings remediated, reduces the risk of token-level vulnerabilities
The recently completed product-related audit with a full relevancy score strengthens assurance over key controls.
The bug bounty program was updated last month

reviews.text: ZKSync is a layer-2 rollup on Ethereum using zk-proofs for fast, cheap transactions. Launched in 2020 by Matter Labs, it evolved into ZKSync Era for full EVM compatibility. In 2025, it’s widely used for DeFi and NFTs with native account abstraction. The team is active with upgrades. It’s a top L2 option.

ZKsync is a layer 2 scaling solution for eth developed by matter labs. Technology zk rollup zk snark/zk evm. In 2023, the ZK era was reached and the mainnet was activated in March 2023. Founding CEO Alex Gluchowski. I actively used it for a period before and after mainnet. The currency is ZK.

zkSync (Matter Labs’ product) is another Ethereum Layer-2 that uses ZK-rollup proofs. It gained attention with its 2025 Atlas upgrade delivering ~15,000 TPS throughput, sub-second finality, and ~$0.0001 fees. Atlas boosted total zk-rollup TVL to over $3.5B, drawing enterprises like Deutsche Bank and UBS and even caused a ~50% surge in the ZK token after Vitalik’s endorsement. zkSync seems to be a next-gen Ethereum accelerator with insane speed. It recently expanded on multiple chains and introduced token staking for network incentives.

ZKsync is a high speed and low price EVM compatible Ethereum layer2 scaling solution that uses Zero Knowledge Succinct Non Interactive Arguments of Knowledge (ZK-SNARKs) proof to validate transactions. ZKsync has a native account abstraction capability and ZK Stack, a custom interconnected ZK Rollups that recently gave rise to Prividum, a private permissioned Blockchain infrastructure for financial institutions and enterprises that require privacy and regulatory compliance. Zksync was developed by experienced team members that contributed to ZK and Ethereum Community. The protocol is backed by top tier VCs like a16z,Blockchain capital, Dragonfly and Coinbase Ventures. However, Complexities associated with ZK rollup Z competition from other layer 2s are the major causes of concern about the project.

ZKsync feels like one of the most promising Ethereum L2s to me it’s fully EVM compatible and uses ZK proofs for scaling, which is as good as it gets for security plus speed. Its recent upgrades like “Atlas” have smashed speed records tens of thousands of TPS at tiny fees and it’s attracting billions in deposits. My only worry is that its token has been very volatile: it tanked about 60% even as usage grew, showing that market sentiment is still fragile.

zkSync is one of those Layer2 projects that came in with a lot of hype. The idea is strong fast, cheap transactions using zk rollups, and staying fully aligned with Ethereum’s security. The team has been pushing hard, and you can see they’re trying to build something big.
But at the same time, zkSync feels a bit inconsistent. Some days the network runs smooth, other days things feel slow or buggy. The ecosystem is growing, but not as fast as people expected, especially after all the early hype. The tech is impressive, no doubt, but the overall experience still feels like it needs more polish.
Still, zkSync is definitely a serious L2 with a real team behind it it just needs time to stabilize and catch up with user expectations.
